<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
`fixFileWithRules` already skips the fix call when violations are empty.

The rule itself needs a documented no-op for `fix(ctx, [])`. I will make `nestedRule.fix` return unchanged content when violations are empty, document the contract, and add a test.

Unused analyzer re-exports will be removed. The fixer re-export of `applyNestedOnly` will also be deleted if it is unused. `transformNestedBlocks` preserves the AST when no violations exist, but the printer may still normalize whitespace.

The no-op fix will return `ctx.parsedFile.content` directly, bypassing the printer entirely. Since `index.ts` re-exports the analyzer, `findNestedViolations` remains part of the public API and must stay exported.

Removing the analyzer re-export would break the public API, since `index.ts` only re-exports the analyzer. The bead permits removing thin re-exports only if callers can import directly from the nested module. No internal callers depend on the analyzer re-export, but external consumers would need to import from `nested-violation-detector` instead.

I am checking whether `nested-rule` should explicitly implement the `ViolationRule` type and whether documentation should be deepened.

The no-op guard belongs on `nestedRule.fix`, not inside `applyNestedOnly`. I will check `docs/rule-pipeline-architecture.md` and review the parallel 5x2.1.1 work for consistent patterns.
</details></think>
